body.heading: An anchor for a drifting mind
paragraphs: When your thoughts are racing ahead — replaying, predicting, worrying — your senses are one of the quickest ways back to the present moment. The five-senses exercise is a well-known grounding technique used in mindfulness practice.
Start with sight. Name five things you can see, slowly and specifically: not just “a tree,” but “the chipped green paint on the gate.” Specific detail is what holds your attention in place.

body.heading: Continue through the senses
paragraphs: Then four things you can hear, three you can touch, two you can smell, and one you can taste. There is no score and no way to do it wrong; drifting off and coming back is the exercise.
The whole thing takes about a minute and works almost anywhere — a bus, a classroom, a queue. It will not solve the problem you are worried about, but it can return you to it a little steadier.

takeaway: Five things you can see: the simplest way back to right now.
